summary: onSave is now async and writes the whole store to data/notes.json after each save. Its caller in the router and HTTP server still treats the return value as a string.

findings.title: Async onSave breaks synchronous dispatch caller
findings.problem: dispatch in src/router.js:7 returns the promise from onSave without awaiting it. The server in src/main.js:9 then passes that promise to res.end, which accepts only a string or Buffer.
findings.consequence: Node throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE inside the request listener, and this uncaught exception crashes the server on every POST /save request. A writeFile rejection also goes unhandled, because no caller awaits the promise or attaches a catch.
findings.fix: Make dispatch async and await the handler. In main.js, await dispatch inside an async listener and catch errors to send a 500 response.

findings.title: Snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: onSave now writes the store to disk and returns a promise. The repository has no test that covers this behaviour.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions like the broken caller in the router and HTTP server.
findings.fix: Add a test that calls dispatch for a save. The test should check the response text and the snapshot file contents.
